purpose: Persistent learning log for the Crown Royales CFB + NFL betting model.
principles: Keep Crown Royal rare and reserved for the highest-conviction setup.
Use moneylines or alternate spreads for higher-stake core bets when the full market spread creates unnecessary variance.
Keep the Hail Mary separate from the core card; target roughly $300-$500 from a $10 stake.
Track both parlay outcomes and individual leg hit rates so a one-leg miss is still informative.
Avoid overfitting to one week; adjust only when misses reveal repeatable risk such as overaggressive road-favorite spreads, uncertain touchdown dependence, or fragile volume assumptions.

results.lesson: Texas won 20-17 but failed to cover -5.5. The ticket's only miss came from asking a favored team to cover rather than simply win. For core/high-stake tickets, favor ML or alt-spread protection when price permits.
Shorter protected parlay structure worked; preserve this format for higher-stake CFB tickets.
Do not let injury-based matchup edges overwhelm turnover/game-variance risk. Crown Royal confidence should require multiple independent edges, not one dominant narrative.
Protected favorites performed better than the outright Crown Royal call; continue separating confidence tier from payout attractiveness.
Volume-based receiving thresholds are preferable to touchdown-dependent props for the Lock Prop.
TD props and aggressive alt thresholds added too much variance. Keep Hail Mary around 5-6 legs and diversify between sides, volume props, and only a limited number of TD scorers.
